transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Hello. I'm here because I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. It feels like I'm just going through the motions without any real spark left.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

These feelings have been going on pretty steadily for about eight months now. It really all started when I was passed over for a long-anticipated promotion to a tenure-track position, even though I had put in years of extra work and effort for the department.
Along with this loss of interest, have you experienced other changes like trouble sleeping, changes in your appetite, or feeling constantly fatigued?

Yes, my sleep has been awful—I lie awake for hours replaying work emails, or I wake up around 3 AM with a heavy, anxious feeling and can't fall back asleep. Because of that, I'm constantly exhausted and foggy during the day, though my appetite hasn't really changed.
Along with the loss of interest, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or empty most of the day, or experienced feelings of worthlessness and self-blame?

Yes, I feel this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest almost constantly, like there's a gray film over everything that doesn't lift even when good things happen. Ever since I missed that promotion, I've also felt like a fraud and a disappointment, constantly blaming myself and feeling like my husband and students would be better off with someone more competent.
Have you ever experienced a period of deep sadness, loss of interest, or exhaustion like this at any other point in your life before?
No, I haven't. This is the first time in my life that I've ever felt this way, and it's all very new and overwhelming.
You mentioned feeling like your husband and students would be better off without you. Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

On my worst days, especially after a long, unproductive evening at my desk, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up or could quietly slip away. I don't have any plan to hurt myself and I've never tried to act on those thoughts, but the feeling of just wanting to disappear is definitely there.
To what extent have these feelings of sadness, exhaustion, and brain fog interfered with your actual ability to perform your teaching duties, connect with your students, or engage with your husband?

It has interfered tremendously; I’ve fallen behind on grading, started canceling student art activities, and I find myself dragging into class feeling completely exhausted and foggy. I'm also avoiding department events, and at home, my husband has had to take over most of the household chores because I just don't have the energy to keep up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with her first episode of a depressive disorder, characterized by a depressed mood, marked anhedonia, insomnia (early morning awakening), fatigue, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, cognitive difficulties (brain fog), and passive suicidal ideation. These symptoms have persisted for eight months following a significant psychosocial stressor (being passed over for a promotion) and have caused severe functional impairment in her professional and domestic life. There is no prior history of depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes.
